explanations: problemHandler looks up mappers by err.name. Every error class sets this.name except CarrierUnavailableError, whose constructor only calls super(...). Its name therefore stays "Error", no mapper matches, and a carrier outage is answered with a generic 500 and no Retry-After header instead of 503 with Retry-After. Clients cannot tell a transient carrier problem from a server bug, and the retry hint is lost. Setting this.name = "CarrierUnavailableError" (or mapping by instanceof) fixes it.

InvalidStateTransitionError sets its name, so mappers["InvalidStateTransitionError"] matches and builds status 409 with detail `${from} -> ${to} is not allowed`. 404 is for missing shipments, 422 is used for address rejection, and 204 is only sent when cancel succeeds.

The first line checks res.headersSent and calls next(err), handing the error to express's default handler, which closes the connection rather than writing a second response. It does not write a problem body (headers are already sent), does not swallow the error, and never re-runs the route.

instance is set to req.originalUrl, identifying this occurrence, while type is a stable identifier for the problem kind that clients can switch on. The status has its own field, and no stack trace is ever included in the body.
